subject: Why is the default arg. "permuted = TRUE" in extract()? (rstan)

messages.author: a2bfdf24157fa01a
messages.subject: Why is the default arg. "permuted = TRUE" in extract()? (rstan)
parts:
Hello all,

I was hoping to get some help understanding why the default behavior of the extract function in rstan is to randomize the order of the samples (permuted = TRUE). EDIT: It seems this is a long-standing issue that has cropped up repeatedly. (e.g., from 2014 - https://groups.google.com/d/msg/stan-users/U3mTZjnqYhI/g4ngytCg81MJ)

In my opinion, this is really dangerous behavior because:

1. It is unexpected (even if it is sensible).

2. It destroys autocorrelation in the extracted samples, which will give misleading ESS estimates for quantities that are derived using the extracted samples.

3. If you are using rstan to work with CSV files generated by cmdstan, the permutation is a random quantity generated when read_stan_csv() is called, not when the model is run. Hence, it will change each time the CSVs are read into R, which is less than ideal (see #1).

If it is worth keeping as the default, can we update the docs to warn cmdstan users that they will need to over-ride it or set a seed prior to READING the data into R, not prior to calling extract()? Alternatively, can the permutation be set from the model seed, so it will not change each time the CSVs are imported?

Thanks,

Matt

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Why is the default arg. "permuted = TRUE" in extract()? (rstan)
parts: It is dangerous. We will probably change it or render it obsolete for rstan3. It was put in because Andrew thought it would prevent people from doing dangerous things on a subset of the draws, but no one really uses a subset of the draws very often.
